records.title: Minimal essentials for humanized vessel-on-a-chip model for vascular research.
records.abstract: During the last decade, in vitro 3D models based on organ-on-a-chip technology have been developed, representing a biotechnology research advance towards more physiologically relevant models that aim to provide more predictable and less costly preclinical models. We aimed to develop a vessel-on-a-chip using a biocompatible microfluidic device co-cultured with human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMC). VSMC and HUVEC were isolated from umbilical cords and co-cultured in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) chip using specific growth media and tropoelastin-enriched media to favour extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis, which was measured by gene expression (quantitative polymerase chain reaction) and deposition (immunofluorescence), to establish an organized structure. Then, using a microfluidic pump system, the functional relevance of the model was evaluated by fluidic and permeability studies after a 9-day- cell growth period. Our vessel-on-a-chip model showed a bilayer structure, cell specific morphology and biomarkers phenotypes, and cell integrity. Gene and protein expression demonstrated the presence of ECM components, providing structural support and microenvironment control. It was observed that shear stress closer to the physiological range provided stability to the model and control of the permeability function. Our 3D model may serve as a promising preclinical research tool that closely mimics the structural conformation of blood vessels and reflects essential physiological parameters, including cell maturity, shear stress, and functional permeability. Consequently, it could potentially be applied to cellular and molecular research to further elucidate vascular biology in cardiovascular diseases.

records.title: Granular hydrogel bioink for macroporous pancreatic spheroid scaffolds.
records.abstract: Cells positioned more than several hundred microns away from a vascular network experience insufficient oxygen and nutrient supply due to diffusion limitations, leading to compromised viability and impaired function. This challenge is especially relevant in large, engineered 3D constructs which exceed the diffusion limitation of 100 - 200 µm, resulting in necrotic cores. Granular hydrogels have emerged as a promising approach for tissue engineering due to their inherent porosity. Their interconnected pores can facilitate mass transport of oxygen and nutrients, and therefore support cellular function. In this work, we developed a facile method to prepare bioprintable granular hydrogel bioink containing microparticles with tunable diameters, that can form porous scaffolds with different pore sizes and porosities. The bioink remained shelf-stable for at least 60 days when stored at 4 °C, as determined by the melt temperature. The macroporous granular hydrogel scaffold has inherent void spaces between the hydrogel microparticles, in which spheroids can be embedded. Pancreatic spheroids incorporated into the scaffold showed improved viability compared to free spheroids, indicating the granular microenvironment supports spheroid survival. Furthermore, functional studies of embedded pancreatic spheroids with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) demonstrated preserved insulin secretion functionality. Our approach thus serves as a tunable platform for supporting the culture of functional spheroids and organoids, that has potential regenerative medicine applications in restoration of physiological functions when implanted.

records.title: What Does a Donor Need to Know? Content Analysis of Informed Consent Documents Used for Brain Organoid Research.
records.abstract: Donors of cells used to create induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and brain organoids may not understand what brain organoids are, how they will be used, or the long-term implications of the research. Informed consent documents (ICDs) often contain highly technical language and are written at reading grade levels higher than those attained by the target population. Our goal was to evaluate informed consent documents used for brain organoid research. We compared 20 currently active, IRB-approved consent documents to published templates/guidelines for iPSC research consent. Analyzed ICDs adhered to guidelines in explaining risks and benefits, de-identification, commercial potential, storage, and results sharing. However, descriptions of current and future use were lacking in detail, and the average reading level of ICDs far exceeded that of the general population. Our findings suggest additional transparency in ICDs would assist participants in making an informed choice about participation in iPSC and brain organoid research.

records.title: From organoids to assembloids: modeling tissue crosstalk in female reproductive biology and disease.
records.abstract: The female reproductive tract is a multi-tissue system in which epithelial, stromal, immune, and vascular cells coordinate responses to hormonal signals. Single-tissue organoids have advanced epithelial modeling in vitro but cannot capture the inter-tissue communication underlying key reproductive processes. Assembloids, which recombine cells from distinct tissue compartments in three-dimensional space, offer a means to restore these missing interactions. This review examines reproductive assembloid research across three biology-driven contexts. In menstrual cycle modeling, organoid-based systems have recapitulated epithelial breakdown and regeneration, yet stromal, immune, and vascular integration remain incomplete. In implantation modeling, embryo-endometrial co-cultures and receptive assembloids have begun to capture maternal-fetal crosstalk, though immune and vascular dimensions are largely missing. In endometriosis and adenomyosis modeling, assembloids have started to reconstruct pathogenic microenvironments that single organoids cannot replicate. Three issues are examined in depth. The first is the gap between what current models can and cannot reveal about reproductive biology. The second is the risk that added complexity may only confirm findings already established in vivo. The third is the point at which an additional tissue component stops contributing new information. Progress in this field is likely to depend not on greater structural complexity but on questions that only multi-tissue models can address.

records.title: Microphysiological organ-on-a-chip system for anti-doping research: long-term CYP activity characterization and S107 metabolism in a HepaRG™-based 3D liver model.
records.abstract: Identification of metabolic markers of prohibited and emerging performance-enhancing substances remains a key challenge in anti-doping analysis, where limitations of conventional in vitro models in resembling authentic physiological conditions exist. Organ-on-a-chip (OoC) systems combining 3D human liver-cell cultures with microfluidic perfusion offer a predictive alternative for human-like drug metabolism. In this study, a HepaRG™-based liver OoC model incorporating hepatic stellate cells was characterized over a three-week period with a focus on cytochrome P450 (CYP)-mediated metabolism. CYP activity, gene expression, and inducibility were assessed for major hepatic CYP isoforms, complemented by pharmacogenomic profiling. Metabolic performance was further evaluated using S107, a non-approved and prohibited doping agent, with metabolite formation being determined by liquid chromatography and high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) in comparison with published in vitro data. The OoC system maintained stable viability and hepatic functionality throughout the culture period, demonstrating phase-I metabolic competence. Isoform-specific differences in mRNA expression and enzymatic activity highlighted complex regulatory effects within the microphysiological environment, while rifampicin responses confirmed preserved nuclear receptor-mediated inducibility across the system. Functional limitations were observed for CYP2D6 and CYP2B6, which showed absent or restricted activity despite detectable transcriptional signals. For S107, the model generated both phase-I and phase-II metabolites, consistent with literature data from microsomal incubation experiments. Metabolite formation was stable over the three-week period under dynamic perfusion conditions, demonstrating sustained biotransformation capacity. Overall, the HepaRG™ OoC system represents a physiologically relevant in vitro platform for long-term metabolism and demonstrates potential as a predictive tool for anti-doping applications and for elucidating metabolic pathways of emerging performance-enhancing substances.

records.title: Low-order lateral transducer modes enabling millimeter-scale acoustofluidics.
records.abstract: Bulk acoustic wave devices commonly use thickness modes of piezoelectric plates to generate standing waves in microfluidic cavities, typically at 2 MHz and above, with corresponding wavelengths well below the millimeter scale. However, handling larger mesoscopic objects-such as organoids and small model organisms, including nematodes-requires millimeter-scale fluidic structures. Single-node alignment in such cavities demands half-wavelength fields and thus sub-megahertz actuation. Conventional sub-megahertz operation requires thicker piezoelectric plates, resulting in bulky designs or requiring plate thicknesses that are not readily available commercially. Here, we demonstrate a practical yet elegant alternative based on a low-order lateral extensional mode of the transducer plate. Compared with thickness-mode devices of identical footprint, the approach lowers the operating frequency approximately fourfold and increases the channel cross section sixteenfold. Unlike typical Lamb-wave devices based on multiwavelength propagation at several megahertz and above, the present approach uses a low-order standing S0 Lamb mode. The numerically optimized devices operate at approximately 540 kHz and achieve rapid particle focusing in millimeter-wide channels, while vibrometry confirms the predicted vibration patterns and admittance measurements show that the lateral resonance is well preserved upon chip loading, with only a small, predictable shift in resonance frequency. The present study focuses on modal characterization and particle-focusing validation. Practical limitations include heating at high actuation voltages and the finite lifetime of the liquid acoustic coupling layer.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: APR-Score: Identification and Scoring of Aggregation-prone Regions in Protein Sequences.
records.abstract: Protein aggregation is a critical phenomenon associated with numerous neurodegenerative and systemic diseases. Understanding the propensity of proteins to aggregate is essential for unraveling the molecular basis of these disorders and for the design and engineering of novel proteins, as well as for modulating the activity/stability of enzymatic proteins. Here, we present APR-Score, a novel machine learning-based computational method designed to identify aggregation-prone regions within protein sequences. APR-Score leverages a combination of sequence-based features to predict regions of proteins that are prone to aggregation. It harnessed the information embedded in compiled sequence and structural features to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy. The method was evaluated through rigorous cross-validation on the training dataset and further validated on an independent test dataset. APR-Score demonstrated robustness and reliability in distinguishing aggregation-prone regions from non-aggregating ones, achieving a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.77, precision of 0.89, and F1-Score of 0.87. This tool offers significant value for researchers investigating protein aggregation-related diseases, as it can expedite the identification of aggregation-prone regions, thereby aiding the development of targeted therapies and diagnostic tools. Moreover, computational protein design and engineering efforts can be facilitated by APR-Score-based identification and screening of aggregation-prone protein sequences. APR-Score is available at https://github.com/TII-BRC/APR-Score.

records.title: HDAC8 Assistant: a QSAR-guided molecular generation platform for de novo design and virtual screening of HDAC8 inhibitors.
records.abstract: Histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) inhibitors are considered promising therapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer and several other diseases. In this study, regression QSAR models for HDAC8 inhibitors were developed using various types of molecular descriptors and machine learning algorithms. The best-performing weighted consensus model achieved an external predictive performance of Q2test = 0.62 for the complete test set and 0.71 for compounds within the applicability domain, covering 77% of the external data. Model reliability was confirmed by five-fold cross-validation and y-randomization tests. The developed QSAR model was integrated into the HDAC8 Assistant web application (https://hdac8-assistant.streamlit.app/), which includes a de novo molecular generation module based on recurrent neural networks (SMILES-RNN) and reinforcement learning (REINVENT 2). For targeted discovery of novel inhibitors, an original reward function was proposed that combines QSAR-predicted activity with applicability domain control for generated compounds. This approach enables simultaneous optimization of predicted inhibitory activity while limiting extrapolation beyond the model applicability domain. HDAC8 Assistant also implements assessment of drug-likeness according to the Muegge criteria, as well as PAINS, toxicophore, and Brenk structural-alert detection. Molecular docking was performed for the most promising compounds generated by HDAC8 Assistant to analyse their interactions with the HDAC8 active site.

records.title: Programming biological behavior with AI-guided de novo protein design.
records.abstract: Driven by advances in artificial intelligence, de novo protein design can now generate diverse molecular functions from the ground up, achieving remarkable success in engineering binders against many macromolecular targets. Here, we provide a perspective on how de novo design can progress beyond bimolecular interactions toward the bottom-up construction of protein reaction networks. We highlight how programmable, modular, and controllable de novo components can drive complex, emergent biological behaviors. Overcoming current challenges-including designable protein dynamics, multi-step functionalities, and non-equilibrium systems-is essential for this transition. With continued foundational method improvements, the field is poised to pioneer precise protein perturbations for systems-level insight and to engineer emergent cellular behaviors like signal amplification, decision-making, and error correction de novo to fundamentally advance synthetic biology, biotechnology, and medicine.

records.title: Multi-Objective Molecular Generation via Actor-Critic Regulated by Adaptive Cooperative Evolution.
records.abstract: Many complex diseases involve intricate and interdependent biological mechanisms, making multi-target drug design therapeutically important. However, existing molecular generation models often struggle to balance conflicting property requirements, maintain structural exploration, and avoid premature convergence during reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose CMIR-RL, a reinforcement learning-based molecular generation model that integrates cooperative crossover-mutation exploration, structure-based intrinsic rewards, and Pareto-based multi-objective optimization. In CMIR-RL, mutation and crossover networks synergistically guide the agent to balance exploration and exploitation, while Pareto-front-guided reward assignment updates the generation policy under multiple property constraints. Experiments on a three-objective polypharmacology task show that CMIR-RL significantly improves desirability from 0.8868 to 0.9542 over the baseline method, while maintaining competitive validity, uniqueness, and diversity. Additional GuacaMol results further indicate competitive generalization across goal-directed molecular generation tasks. These results show that CMIR-RL is an effective reinforcement learning strategy for early-stage multi-objective molecular design.
records.journal: IEEE transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics

records.title: Virus-like particle vaccines: from antigen architecture to antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses.
records.abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs) mimic key structural features of native viruses while lacking a replication-competent viral genome, combining favorable safety with multivalent antigen presentation and strong immunogenicity. Yet, how VLP design influences the quality and persistence of adaptive immunity remains incompletely understood. This review examines relevant literature identified through targeted searches on recent advances in VLP engineering, with emphasis on particle architecture, antigen-display strategies, and structural determinants of immune recognition. We discuss how VLPs facilitate antigen presentation by antigen-presenting cells and shape CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses, immune memory, and T follicular helper cell-B-cell interactions within germinal centers. Emerging approaches linking VLP design with humoral and cellular immunity are also considered. The next generation of VLP vaccines will require a transition from empirical enhancement of immunogenicity toward precision engineering of immune responses. A major challenge is to establish robust and transferable structure-immunity relationships while addressing manufacturing feasibility, quality control, potency assessment, and product comparability. Advances in computational protein design, structural biology, and high-dimensional immune profiling are expected to enable increasingly quantitative and mechanism-based optimization of VLP platforms. However, fully predictive control over human immune responses will remain a complex challenge.

records.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
records.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A cost-ordered cascade concentrates full structure-based evaluation on a small pre-filtered survivor set, achieving a 2.5 × reduction in candidates advanced relative to those generated. An in-loop metabolic gate enforces Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) safety by writing flagged reactive substructures to a per-target learned state, suppressing identified liabilities from all subsequent generation rounds. A persistent campaign memory influences generation trajectories by embedding prior structural success and failure patterns directly into the design context. We validate these architectural invariants across three structurally diverse benchmark targets (EGFR, KRAS G 12 C , and BRD4) through a five-condition component ablation and a controlled memory ablation, and confirm generator agnosticism across four language-model backends via a deterministic recalibration layer that overrides backend self-evaluation bias. Without explicit chemotype instruction, the pipeline computationally converged toward candidates bearing the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold characteristic of the approved inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, from structural feedback alone. Persistent campaign memory showed directional but non-significant trends toward lower inter-round score variance and higher late-stage advance rate ( n ≈ 90 per condition; all p > 0.20 ). The component ablation reveals that optimizing for a single objective collapses performance on others; only full orchestration resolves this tension. Advancement rates above 79% across all backends confirm that the validated properties are generator-agnostic, enforced by architectural invariants rather than model capability. All reported outcomes are properties of the computational generation process; prospective biochemical validation of the advanced candidates remains the primary direction for future work.

records.title: [Advances on Postoperative Recurrence Risk Prediction in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
records.abstract: Lung cancer remains the malignant tumor with the highest incidence and mortality rates worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for approximately 85% of cases. Radical surgical resection serves as the primary curative modality for patients with resectable NSCLC; however, postoperative recurrence persists in a subset of patients, thereby compromising long-term survival outcomes. Consequently, the precise prediction of postoperative recurrence risk, identification of high-risk populations, and formulation of individualized adjuvant therapy and surveillance strategies are of paramount importance for improving patient prognosis. In recent years, fueled by the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and liquid biopsy technologies, the prediction of postoperative recurrence in NSCLC has progressively transitioned toward greater precision and personalization. This review summarizes the current applications of traditional predictive models, AI-based models, and liquid biopsy techniques in forecasting NSCLC recurrence following surgery, evaluating their respective strengths and limitations. Furthermore, it provides insights into future research trajectories. .

records.title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound: Established and Emerging Applications in Neurosciences.
records.abstract: Transcranial MR-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) thermoablation is an established incisionless image-guided treatment for movement disorders; however, neuroradiologist involvement in clinical decision-making and procedural workflows is highly variable and site-specific. Transcranial low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) is a rapidly evolving non-invasive, image-guided technology for neuromodulation and blood-brain barrier disruption. Compared with HIFU, the optimal protocol, therapeutic mechanism, and safety limits remain uncertain for LIFU. Despite these gaps, LIFU has significant potential for neuropsychiatric and neuro-oncologic diseases. Familiarity with transcranial ultrasound principles and the pivotal role of CT and MR imaging for targeting and evaluating outcomes is increasingly important for neuroradiologists. This review uses HIFU as a clinical model to illustrate the integration of imaging into focused ultrasound workflows. We then discuss LIFU with respect to technical factors, imaging considerations, safety, and limitations. We highlight its emerging applications, including neuromodulation, targeted drug delivery, and liquid biopsy. Finally, we conclude by summarizing key knowledge gaps, outlining future directions, and proposing strategies to more actively engage neuroradiologists in this emerging field.

records.title: Exhaled Breath Analysis for Lung Cancer Detection: From VOCs Signatures to EBC-Based Liquid Biopsy and Clinical Translation.
records.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Although low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is the current standard for early screening, its high false-positive rates and cumulative radiation exposure create a pressing clinical need for complementary, non-invasive diagnostic tools. Exhaled breath analysis represents an accessible strategy for early detection and risk stratification. Early breathomics primarily focused on gas-phase volatile organic compounds (VOCs). However, as volatile metabolites, VOCs are chemically unstable and highly susceptible to background ambient air and physiological confounders. Distinct from gas-phase analysis, exhaled breath condensate (EBC) offers enhanced biomarker stability and functions as a lung-proximal liquid biopsy. By capturing non-volatile, high-molecular-weight analytes, including tumor-derived nucleic acids and proteins, EBC more closely reflects the underlying molecular mechanisms of the respiratory microenvironment. Nevertheless, the clinical translation of EBC remains constrained by severe sample dilution, unstandardized collection device architectures, and pre-analytical inconsistencies. This review summarizes the progression from VOCs profiling to EBC-based platforms, detailing recent advances in sample harvesting, ultrasensitive detection technologies, and multi-omics integration. Advancing EBC toward routine clinical use requires consensus-driven standard operating procedures and the application of machine learning algorithms to high-dimensional datasets. Future efforts should prioritize large-scale, multicenter prospective trials to validate specific EBC signatures, thereby establishing this technology as a reliable liquid biopsy for precision pulmonary oncology.

records.title: Potential clinical significance of soluble and extracellular vesicle-bound HER2 in breast cancer.
records.abstract: HER2, a member of the epidermal growth factor receptor family, is a cell surface protein that plays a critical role in the development of aggressive breast cancer phenotypes and serves as a molecular target for HER2-directed therapy. The extracellular domain of HER2 undergoes proteolytic shedding into the bloodstream, generating a circulating pool of soluble HER2. In parallel, circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs, including tumor-derived EV subpopulations) have emerged as a distinct liquid biopsy compartment, preserving full-length, membrane-anchored HER2 on their surface. This review summarizes current evidence on the clinical relevance of blood soluble HER2 and extracellular vesicle-bound HER2 levels in breast cancer. Particular emphasis is placed on their potential as surrogate markers of HER2-positive disease, prognostic indicators, predictors of response to systemic therapies, and an additional parameter for patient monitoring aimed at the preclinical detection of disease progression. Analysis of accumulated data indicates that soluble HER2 measurement cannot currently be recommended for routine clinical decision-making. At the same time, the consistent association between elevated soluble HER2 levels and poor prognosis in breast cancer supports further investigation of this biomarker. The recently developed analytical approaches for extracellular vesicle-bound HER2 are demonstrating complementary value as liquid biopsy tools. Identifying patient subgroups in which soluble HER2 and extracellular vesicle-bound HER2 may provide the greatest clinical utility will be essential for realizing their full diagnostic and prognostic potential.

records.title: Multi-omics liquid biopsy for leptomeningeal metastases in lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to precision diagnosis and treatment.
records.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM), a serious complication of advanced lung cancer, poses significant challenges in both clinical diagnosis and treatment monitoring, and is associated with a poor prognosis. Conventional diagnostic methods include magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology; however, their sensitivity is limited, particularly in the early stages of the disease. Against this backdrop, liquid biopsy has emerged as a minimally invasive and practical approach for molecular assessment and longitudinal monitoring of LM. Recent studies have reported that, in selected cohorts of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and LM, CSF-derived circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detects driver and resistance-associated alterations more frequently than paired plasma, while epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM)-based CSF circulating tumor cell (CTC) assays have reported sensitivities of 76%-100% and specificities of 84%-100%, compared with a first-lumbar-puncture sensitivity of 44%-67% for conventional CSF cytology. These performance estimates should be interpreted in the context of selected cohorts and heterogeneous reference frameworks. Furthermore, cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumor cell (CSF-CTC) burden holds prognostic value, with higher CTC levels associated with poorer survival outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in liquid biopsy biomarkers including ctDNA, DNA methylation, microRNA (miRNA), proteins, and circulating tumor cells (CTCs), focusing on their applications in the diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and prognostic assessment of lung cancer-associated LM, and provides a comparative discussion of liquid biopsy based on plasma and cerebrospinal fluid specimens. It further explores the potential, current challenges, and directions for clinical translation of multi-omics integration in the personalized management of LM.
